title: A Day on Venus Is Longer Than Its Year
description: On Venus, one full spin takes longer than one trip around the Sun. Here is how that works.

scenes.text: There is a planet where a single day lasts longer than a whole year. And it is our closest neighbor.
Venus turns on its axis incredibly slowly. One full spin takes about two hundred and forty three Earth days.
But it only needs about two hundred and twenty five Earth days to go all the way around the Sun.
It gets stranger. Venus spins the opposite way to most planets, so there the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.
So on Venus, your birthday would come around before the day was even over. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Octopuses Have Three Hearts and Blue Blood
description: Three hearts, blue blood and arms that can taste. The octopus is stranger than you think.

scenes.text: An octopus has three hearts. Not one, not two, but three.
Two of them pump blood through the gills, where it picks up oxygen. The third pumps it around the rest of the body.
And that blood is blue. It uses copper to carry oxygen instead of iron, which is what makes ours red.
Here is the strange part. When an octopus swims, the heart that serves the body stops beating. That is one reason they prefer crawling.
Three hearts, blue blood, and it would rather walk than swim. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Sharks Are Older Than Trees
description: Sharks were swimming the oceans millions of years before the first trees grew on land.

scenes.text: Sharks are older than trees. That sounds wrong, but it is true.
The earliest sharks appeared roughly four hundred and fifty million years ago, in ancient seas.
The first true trees did not show up on land until around three hundred and eighty five million years ago.
That means sharks have survived several mass extinctions, including the one that wiped out the dinosaurs.
The next time you walk through a forest, remember that sharks were here first. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Bananas Are Berries but Strawberries Aren't
description: Botanists have a strict definition of a berry, and it gives some surprising answers.

scenes.text: Is a banana a berry? According to scientists, yes it is.
To a botanist, a berry is a fruit that grows from a single flower with one ovary, and usually holds several seeds inside.
By that rule, bananas, grapes and even tomatoes are berries. But the strawberry is not, because its seeds sit on the outside.
Pumpkins and cucumbers count as a kind of berry too, while raspberries do not.
So the berry aisle has been lying to you. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Cleopatra Lived Closer to the Moon Landing Than the Pyramids
description: The Great Pyramid was already ancient history by the time Cleopatra ruled Egypt.

scenes.text: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the first Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
The Great Pyramid of Giza was built around two thousand five hundred and sixty BC.
Cleopatra died in thirty BC. That is about two and a half thousand years after the pyramid went up.
The Moon landing came in nineteen sixty nine, about two thousand years after her. So the pyramid was ancient even to her.
History is a lot longer than it feels. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Wombats Make Cube-Shaped Poop
description: Wombats are the only animals known to produce cube-shaped droppings. Scientists worked out how.

scenes.text: There is an animal in Australia that makes poop shaped like little cubes. It is the wombat.
For years, nobody knew how it worked. A round tube making square shapes seemed impossible.
Scientists found the answer in the gut. The walls of the wombat's intestine have stiff parts and stretchy parts, which press the waste into flat sides and corners.
Wombats leave their droppings on rocks and logs to mark territory. Cubes are less likely to roll away.
Nature really does think outside the box. Follow for more weird facts.

title: There Are More Chess Games Than Atoms in the Universe
description: The number of possible chess games is so big it beats the number of atoms in the observable universe.

scenes.text: There are more possible games of chess than there are atoms in the observable universe.
Scientists estimate the observable universe holds about ten to the power of eighty atoms. That is a one followed by eighty zeros.
A famous estimate puts the number of possible chess games at around ten to the power of one hundred and twenty.
That is not a little bigger. It is forty extra zeros. Every game you play is almost certainly one that has never been played before.
So your next game of chess might be history in the making. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Honey Can Last for Thousands of Years
description: Archaeologists have found honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that had not rotted. Here is why honey lasts.

scenes.text: Archaeologists have found pots of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs, thousands of years old, and it had not rotted.
Honey is mostly sugar with very little water. Bacteria trying to live in it get the water pulled right out of them.
It is also slightly acidic, and bees add an enzyme that helps produce a little hydrogen peroxide, which fights germs.
The trick is keeping it sealed. If honey soaks up moisture from the air, it can start to spoil.
Thank the bees for one of the longest lasting foods on Earth. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Oxford University Is Older Than the Aztec Empire
description: Teaching at Oxford began long before the Aztecs founded their great capital city.

scenes.text: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.
There is evidence of teaching at Oxford as early as ten ninety six, more than nine hundred years ago.
The Aztecs founded their capital city, Tenochtitlan, in thirteen twenty five. That is over two hundred years later.
So students were already studying in Oxford long before one of the most famous empires in the Americas even began.
Our timelines overlap in ways school never mentioned. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Butterflies Taste With Their Feet
description: A butterfly can tell if a leaf is right for its eggs just by standing on it.

scenes.text: Butterflies can taste with their feet.
They have special taste sensors on their legs. The moment they land on something, they can tell what it is made of.
This matters most for mothers. A female butterfly drums her feet on a leaf to check if it is the right plant for her caterpillars to eat.
If the taste is wrong, she flies off and keeps searching. Her babies depend on that tiny foot test.
Imagine tasting your dinner by stepping on it. Follow for more weird facts.
